title: l says /l/
parentNote: Today is /lll/: the tongue tip goes up behind the top teeth and stays there humming while the air slides out around the sides. Two things usually go wrong. The first is that /l/ turns into a /w/ — "lamp" comes out "wamp" — which is a tongue that never went up; ask to see the tongue touch the spot, then say it. The second is that children add a vowel and say "luh", which makes "lip" into "luh-ip"; hold the sound instead, lllll, like a hum. You will also meet a double l today, in words like hill and fill. Two letters, one sound — English simply likes to double l, f and s at the end of a short word, and there is nothing to work out. If they try to say it twice, cover the second l with your thumb and let them read it, then take your thumb away and show them it sounds the same.

activities.mouthCue: Tongue tip up behind your top teeth and leave it there — the hum comes out round the sides.
